name: Kannayariamudayar Temple, Thirukkarayil
deity: Shiva as Kannayiranathar, with Parvati as Kailasanayaki
significance: A medieval Chola-period Shiva temple of the Tiruvarur delta country, counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams hymned in the Tevaram. Devotees seek the deity here for relief from planetary afflictions.
story: Brahma is said to have raised a sand linga here to be freed of the curse he earned by falsely claiming to have found the crown of Shiva's cosmic flame.

name: Nadutariappar Temple, Kanrappur
deity: Shiva as Nadutariappar, with Parvati as Srivalli Nayagi
significance: An 11th-century Chola temple near Tiruvarur with a five-tiered rajagopuram, honoured in the Tevaram hymns of Appar and counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: A Shaiva woman whose husband smashed her linga worshipped a carpenter's wedge instead; when he swung an axe at it, Shiva manifested from the wedge, giving the deity his name.

name: Manathunainathar Temple, Valivalam
deity: Shiva as Manathunainathar, with Parvati as Maazhai Onkanni
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (attr. Early Chola king Kocengannan); renovated later
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in Tevaram hymns by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, and traditionally attributed to the Early Chola king Kocengannan. It is classed as a Madakkoil, built raised so that an elephant cannot climb its steps.

name: Kaichineswarar Temple, Kaichinam
deity: Shiva as Kaichineswarar, with Parvati as Palvalai Nayaki
significance: A village Shiva shrine of the Tiruvarur district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram hymns of Sambandar.

name: Vaimoornathar Temple, Tiruvaimur
deity: Shiva as Vaimoornathar
significance: Paadal Petra Sthalam no. 124, a Shiva shrine revered in the 7th-century hymns of the saints Appar and Sambandar.
story: Tradition holds that the Chola king Mucukunta, choosing rightly among seven identical Thyagaraja images given by Indra, had one of the remaining six installed at Thiruvaimur.

name: Vedaranyeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Vedaranyeswarar
builtDisplay: by early 7th c.; structural temple credited to Aditya Chola (871-907)
significance: The great Shiva temple of Vedaranyam, the ancient Tirumaraikkadu ('forest of the Vedas'), and the only shrine mentioned in all seven Thirumurais of the Tamil Saiva canon. Chola kings from Rajaraja I onward endowed it richly.
story: Its doors, sealed since the Vedas themselves worshipped here, are said to have been sung open by Appar and closed again by Sambandar's hymn.

name: Agastheeswarar Temple, Agasthiyampalli
deity: Shiva as Agastheeswarar, with Parvati as Pakampiriyal Nayagi
builtDisplay: Medieval Chola; Pandya and Nayak additions
significance: A medieval Chola granite temple near Vedaranyam bearing grant inscriptions of Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulothunga I, revered in the Tevaram and classed a Paadal Petra Sthalam.
story: When the earth tilted at Shiva's wedding, sage Agastya was sent south to restore the balance, and Shiva appeared to him here in his marriage form.

name: Kodi Kuzhagar Temple
deity: Shiva as Kuzhagar, with Thadangani Amman
builtDisplay: 9th c. (Chola); inscriptions from Aditya I onward
significance: The land's-end Shiva shrine of Kodikkarai at Point Calimere, a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon carrying Chola inscriptions from Aditya I, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulothunga I.

name: Aappudaiyar Temple, Thiru Aappanoor
deity: Shiva as Aappudaiyar (Rishabareswarar), with Ambal
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam within Madurai city, first raised by Pandya kings and later expanded under the Nayaks and Sethupathis, with a Somaskanda image of note.
story: A carpenter's wedge ('aappu') is said to have turned into a Shivalinga so the Pandya king Solandhagan could cross the flooded Vaigai, naming both temple and deity.

name: Subramaniya Swamy Temple, Thiruparankundram
deity: Murugan (Subramaniya); Shiva as Parangirinathar within the complex
significance: One of the Six Abodes of Murugan, carved into the Thiruparankundram hillock by the Pandyas in the 6th century, with the Shiva shrine of Parangirinathar making it a Paadal Petra Sthalam as well. Nayak-era pillared halls front the ancient cave sanctum.
story: After slaying the asura Surapadman at Tiruchendur, Murugan is said to have married Indra's daughter Deivanai here.

name: Edaganathar Temple
deity: Shiva as Edaganathar, with Parvati as Elavaarkuzhali (Visalakshi)
significance: A Shiva temple on the Vaigai bank northwest of Madurai, founded under the Pandyas with its present masonry raised in the Nayak period, and hymned by Sambandar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: In Sambandar's contest with the Jains, his palm-leaf hymn floated upstream against the Vaigai and landed here, giving Thiruvedagam its name.

name: Kodunkundreeswarar Temple, Piranmalai
deity: Shiva as Kodunkundra Nathar, with Parvati as Thenammal
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (Tevaram era); Marudu-brother additions 18th c.
significance: A hill temple rising in three tiers over Piranmalai, sung by Sambandar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams; the Marudu brothers of Sivaganga were among its later patrons.
story: Piranmalai itself is said to be a block of Mount Meru blown off during the contest between the serpent king Adisesha and the wind god Vayu.

name: Tiruttalinathar Temple, Tiruppattur
deity: Shiva as Tiruttalinathar, with Parvati as Sivakami (Soundarya Nayaki)
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (Tevaram era); patronage from Chola, Pandya and later rulers
significance: Regarded as the sixth of the Tevara sthalams of the Pandya country and one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, with royal patronage running from the early Cholas and Pandyas to the Sethupathis and Marudu Pandiyars.
story: At Mahalakshmi's request, Shiva is said to have revealed his Gowri Thandavam cosmic dance to her at this shrine.

name: Vruddhapureeswarar Temple, Thiruppunavayil
deity: Shiva as Vruddhapureeswarar (Pazhampathinathar)
significance: A coastal-country shrine of Pudukkottai district counted as the seventh of the Pandya-region Tevara sthalams, where Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar each sang the presiding deity.
story: The four Vedas together with Brahma, Vishnu and Lakshmi, Indra, Surya, Chandra and the sages Vasishta and Agastya are all said to have worshipped Shiva here.

name: Adhi Ratneswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Adhi Ratneswarar, with Snehavalli
significance: A major shrine of Ramanathapuram district, one of the fourteen Tevaram-praised Shiva temples of the Pandya country and of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, its gopuram carrying fine Dravidian work.
story: Vaaruni, cursed to bear an elephant's body with a goat's head, is said to have regained his form by worshipping Shiva here, giving Tiruvadanai its name.

name: Sornakaleeswarar (Kaleeswarar) Temple, Kalaiyarkoil
deity: Shiva as Kaleeswarar (Sornakaleeswarar), with Parvati as Swarnambikai
builtDisplay: present temple c. 700 years old; Tevaram-era origins
significance: The great temple of Kalaiyarkoil, ancient Thirukkaanapper, with a 150-foot rajagopuram and three linked Shiva shrines; Sundarar sang its deity, placing it among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The Marudu brothers of Sivaganga later fortified the site.
story: The goddess Kali is said to have worshipped the Kaleeswarar linga here before defeating the demon Chandasura with the seven mothers.

name: Pushpavaneswarar Temple, Tiruppuvanam
deity: Shiva as Pushpavaneswarar, with Parvati as Soundaranayagi
builtDisplay: 7th c. origins; stone temple by Aditya Chola I (870-907)
significance: A Vaigai-bank temple of the Pandya country revered in the Tevaram, its stone structure raised under Aditya I with further Chola endowments from Uttama Chola to Rajendra I recorded in inscriptions.
story: A devoted dancer named Ponanaial is said to have been divinely helped to fashion a golden Shiva idol, on which her pinch-marks remain visible.

name: Thirumeninathar Temple, Thiruchuli
deity: Shiva as Thirumeninathar, with Parvati as Thunaimalaiyammai
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thiruchuli in Virudhunagar district, a Pandya foundation built on the plan of the great Madurai and Rameswaram temples and closely associated with the saint Sundarar.
story: During the great deluge Shiva is said to have swallowed the floodwaters here in a swirl ('chuli'), giving the town its name.

name: Kutralanathar Temple, Courtallam
deity: Shiva as Kutralanathar, with Parvati as Kuzhalvaimozhi Ammai
significance: The temple of Courtallam by its famous waterfalls, laid out on a conch-shaped plan and housing the Chitra Sabha, one of the five cosmic dance halls of Nataraja; Sambandar's Tevaram places it among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: Sage Agastya, unable to attend Shiva's wedding in the north, prayed here and was granted a vision of the lord in full marriage attire.

name: Nellaiappar Temple
deity: Shiva as Nellaiappar (Venuvananathar), with Parvati as Kanthimathi Amman
builtDisplay: 7th c. core (Pandya); walls, halls and gardens added 13th-18th c.
significance: The vast twin temple of Nellaiappar and Kanthimathi dominating Tirunelveli, its sanctums credited to the 7th-century Pandya Nindraseer Nedumaran, with musical pillars and later mandapams spread over nearly six hectares. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon.
story: Vishnu is said to have witnessed the wedding of Shiva and Parvati in the bamboo grove (Venuvana) that gave the deity his name.

name: Avinashiappar Temple (Tiruppukkozhiyur)
deity: Shiva as Avinashiappar (Avinasilingeswarar), with Parvati as Karunambigai
significance: The chief Tevaram shrine of the Kongu country at Avinashi, founded under the Cholas and rebuilt in stone under the Nayaks, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: At Sundarar's hymn, a crocodile is said to have released alive the boy it had swallowed years before, an event replayed each year as the Mudalai Vaai Pillai festival.

name: Thirumuruganatheeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Thirumuruganatheeswarar, with Parvati as Avudainayagi
significance: A 10th-century Kongu Chola temple near Tiruppur, its walls carrying 68 inscriptions of Vikrama Chola, revered in the Tevaram and classed as a garden temple (Kokkudi Koil) among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: Murugan is said to have worshipped his father here to shed the sin of slaying Surapadma, digging a spring with his vel to purify himself.

name: Sangameswarar Temple, Bhavani
deity: Shiva as Sangameswarar, with Vedanayagi
significance: The confluence temple where the Bhavani meets the Kaveri, known in the Tevaram as Thirunana; Sambandar dedicated ten hymns of the second Thirumurai to its deity, and Arunagirinathar later sang its Subramanya.
story: Kubera, flying overhead, is said to have seen a deer, tiger, cow, elephant, snake and rat drinking together beneath an ilandhai tree, revealing the sanctity of the confluence.

name: Ardhanareeswarar Temple, Tiruchengode
deity: Ardhanarishvara, the composite form of Shiva and Parvati
significance: The hill temple of Tiruchengode enshrining Ardhanarishvara, the half-male half-female form of Shiva and Parvati, among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams; Krishnadevaraya raised its Thirumalai gopuram in 1512, and an emerald lingam is among its treasures.
story: When the sage Bhringi circumambulated only Shiva, Parvati performed austerities until the two merged into the single body of Ardhanareeswarar.

name: Vikirtheeswarar Temple, Venjamakoodal
deity: Shiva as Vikriteswarar, with Vikritambika
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Kongu country at Venjamangudalur in Karur district, over twelve centuries old with rock inscriptions of the Pandya period; Sundarar composed a Tevaram pathigam here.
story: Shiva, in the guise of a priest, is said to have blessed Sundarar with gold at this shrine first raised by the hunter-king Venchan.

name: Magudeswarar Temple, Kodumudi
deity: Shiva as Magudeswarar (Kodumudi Nathar), with Parvati as Panmozhi Nayaki
significance: The sixth Tevaram shrine of the Kongu country, on the Kaveri at Kodumudi, sung by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar alike and bearing epigraphs of Pandya rulers including Maravarman Sundarapandian.
story: A crow is said to have tipped over sage Agastya's water-pot here, the spilt water flowing on as the Kaveri to nourish the farmlands downstream.

name: Pasupateeswarar Temple, Karur
deity: Shiva as Pasupateeswarar (Aanilaiappar), with Sundaravalli and Alankaravalli
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (Tevaram era); Chola land grants from Rajendra I
significance: The ancient temple of Karuvoor Aanilai in Karur town, a Paadal Petra Sthalam where Sambandar and Sundarar sang, later endowed by Rajendra Chola and patronised by Kongu Chola, Kongu Pandya and Vijayanagara rulers. Its swayambu lingam stands behind a 120-foot gopuram.
story: The celestial cow Kamadhenu is said to have worshipped the lingam here, and Brahma's worship gave the tank its name Brahma Theertham.

name: Theerthapurisvarar Temple, Tiruvattatthurai
deity: Shiva as Theerthapurisvarar (Aratturainathar), with Anandanayagi
significance: The village shrine of ancient Tirunelvayil Aratturai in Cuddalore district, a Paadal Petra Sthalam where Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar are all held to have worshipped.

name: Sudarkozhundeeswarar Temple, Pennadam
deity: Shiva as Sudarkozhundeeswarar
significance: An early Chola temple at Pennadam whose apsidal sanctum is shaped like an elephant's back (gajaprishthakara), counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and visited by the saint Appar on his pilgrimages.

name: Narthana Vallabeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Narthana Vallabeswarar, with Parvati as Gnanasakthi
significance: A river-confluence shrine of Cuddalore district founded under the Cholas and rebuilt in the Nayak period, glorified by Sundarar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: A Chola king who had wrongfully killed his wife is said to have been cured of the resulting affliction by bathing at the confluence where Shiva rules as Koodalaiyitroorar.

name: Thirukumaresar (Neelakandeswarar) Temple
deity: Shiva as Thirukumaresar (Thiruneelakandeswarar), with Parvati as Verumulai Amman
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of ancient Erukkattampuliyur, birthplace of Tirunilakanta Nayanar of the 63 Nayanmars; the Chola foundation was rebuilt under the Nayaks behind a five-tiered gopuram.
story: Raja Raja Chola is said to have prayed here and been blessed with his son Rajendra, after whom the village was renamed Rajendirapattinam.

name: Veerateeswarar Temple, Thiruvathigai
deity: Shiva as Veerattaaneswarar, with Parvati as Thiripurasundari
significance: One of the eight Veeratta shrines of Shiva, marking his destruction of the three demon cities; here the Pallava king Mahendravarman I embraced Saivism, and the saint Appar returned to the faith and attained salvation. Its seven-tiered gopuram carries early Bharatanatyam sculpture.
story: Shiva is said to have burnt the three flying cities of the asuras from this spot, with Vishnu himself serving as the arrow.

name: Bhaktajaneswarar Temple, Thirunavalur
deity: Shiva as Bhaktajaneswarar, with Parvati as Manonmani Amman
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; Chola origins with Parantaka I inscriptions
significance: The temple of Thirunavalur, home village of the saint-poet Sundarar, with inscriptions running from Parantaka I to Rajendra Chola III; it stands among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Tevaram canon.
story: The shrine's sacred naval tree is traced in legend to a drop spilt during the churning of the ocean of milk.

name: Vriddhagiriswarar Temple, Vriddhachalam
deity: Shiva as Vriddhagiriswarar (Pazhamalai Nadhar), with Viruthambigai (Periyanayaki)
significance: The great temple of Tirumudukunram ('the old hill'), commissioned by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, with five gopurams and a chariot-shaped hundred-pillared hall. A Paadal Petra Sthalam held to grant salvation to departed souls even beyond Varanasi's power.
story: Shiva is said to have taken the form of an ancient mountain at Brahma's prayer, earning the name Pazhamalai, the old hill.

name: Atulya Nadheswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Atulya Nadheswarar, with Parvati as Azhagiya Ponnazhagi
significance: A hill temple above the Thenpennai at Arakandanallur, grown from three Pallava rock-cut caves through Chola expansion to its 16th-century Vijayanagara form, and sung by Sambandar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. Ramana Maharshi is believed to have stayed in its caves before being drawn to Tiruvannamalai.
story: Vishnu is said to have prayed to Shiva here to be cleansed after subduing Mahabali in his Vamana avatar.

name: Marudeeswarar Temple, T. Edaiyar
deity: Shiva as Marudeeswarar (Idayatrunathar), with Parvati as Gnanambigai
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; Chola origins with Rajaraja I inscriptions
significance: A Thenpennai-bank shrine of Viluppuram district revered in the Tevaram of Sambandar and Sundarar, its Chola core recorded in inscriptions of Rajaraja I, Kulothunga I and Rajendra III before a 16th-century rebuilding.
story: The sage who overheard Shiva's secret teaching to Parvati was cursed and, reborn as Vyasa, is said to have won redemption by worshipping here.

name: Kripapureeswarar Temple, Thiruvennainallur
deity: Shiva as Kripapureeswarar (Arutkondanathar), with Parvati as Mangalambigai
builtDisplay: 10th c. (Chola); Sembiyan Mahadevi and Rajaraja I endowments
significance: The 10th-century Chola temple where the saint-poet Sundarar, claimed by Shiva as his slave, began the Tirumurai; it was endowed by queen Sembiyan Mahadevi and Rajaraja I and stands among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: Shiva, appearing as an old man with a palm-leaf bond over Sundarar, revealed himself and bade the saint sing, beginning with the word 'Pitha' - the first verse of the Tevaram.

name: Sishtagurunatheswarar Temple, Tirutturaiyur
deity: Shiva as Sishtagurunatheswarar, with Thyagavalliammai
significance: A village shrine of Cuddalore district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram hymns of the saint Appar.

name: Vadukeeswarar Temple, Thiruvandarkoil
deity: Shiva as Vadukeeswarar, with Parvati as Thiripura Sundari
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; Chola-era origins with Parantaka I inscriptions
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of ancient Thiru Vadukur, now Thiruvandarkoil in Puducherry, its Chola core attested by inscriptions of Parantaka I, Rajaraja I, Kulothunga I and Rajendra III beneath a 16th-century rebuilding.
story: The name Vadukeeswarar - 'he who quivered' - recalls Shiva's severing of the fifth head of a prideful Brahma.
